svg.title: A32: myeloid ARG1, collagen matrix and alveolar epithelial recovery
svg.desc: Hypothesis illustration. A generic myeloid cell contains ARG1, converting arginine to ornithine. The published context-specific matrix premise connects the myeloid metabolite environment to a fibroblast and collagen fibres. A separate alveolar illustration shows cuboidal AT2 cells and thin AT1 epithelium. Dashed comparison arrows denote unmeasured effects of source-restricted ARG1 reduction. Matrix and absolute lineage-derived mature AT1 output must be measured separately. No direction or mediation is established for epithelial recovery. Cell identities, source restriction and the non-infectious model require qualification; source loss and recipient selection remain alternatives.
svg.text: Myeloid ARG1: less matrix, better epithelial recovery?
A joint effect question — the epithelial direction is unresolved.
Source-restricted ARG1 reduction vs matched source-active control
Same qualified non-infectious repair design; model and source-cell identity still to be established.
Two endpoints from one comparison; no assumed matrix → epithelial mediation.
*Context dependent. The complete source–metabolite–matrix pathway is not established in the proposed model.
Less matrix + more mature output: favorable joint effect; less of both: possible tradeoff; uncertain output: unresolved.
source depletion, altered inflammation, direct recipient exposure, or cell survival / selection.
Pending: linked model/data, source restriction, mature-function assay and timing, biological-unit variance and precision.
Original vector illustration • not to scale • published premises: Yadav 2025; Hamanaka 2025 • source detail and limits in LITERATURE_CONTEXT.md
